decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 5.25% to 5.5%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: Job gains have remained strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have moderated since early last year but remain strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low.”

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.47% APR costs about $89.46 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.27% and moved -3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.88% would fall by about $6.01 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 178k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.2% over the past year (February 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -9 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.89%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 90%, cut 10%, hike 0%.

citations.detail: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
